incident: Checkout is intermittently failing with 502s; recommendations pods are restarting.
title: Checkout Service 502 Bad Gateway Incident

root_cause.statement: A mass rollout of multiple shop workloads triggered container runtime resource contention and socket errors, leading to readiness probe failures in downstream dependencies (inventory and recommendations) which propagated upstream as 502s at the checkout and edge layers.

confidence.label: inconclusive
confidence.explanation: Inconclusive: no hypothesis is supported well enough to be called the root cause.

causal_chain.step: Simultaneous rollout of multiple deployments in the shop namespace initiated at 12:21 and 12:26.
Readiness probes for inventory and recommendations pods failed repeatedly due to connection refused and runtime communication issues.
Checkout experienced upstream connection errors and timeouts when attempting to reach downstream dependencies.
Checkout and edge latency increased, resulting in 502 Bad Gateway errors observed by clients.

facts.quote: Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.1.22:8080/readyz": dial tcp 10.244.1.22:8080: connect: connection refused
facts.statement: Widespread readiness probe failures (connection refused) began immediately after the rollout across multiple services.

facts.quote: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = error reading from server: read unix @->/run/containerd/containerd.sock: read: connection reset by peer
facts.statement: The container runtime (containerd) experienced connection resets, failing pod creation and deletion at 12:26:23.

facts.quote: Readiness probe errored and resulted in unknown state: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial unix /run/containerd/containerd.sock: connect: connection refused"
facts.statement: Even the postgres-0 statefulset experienced readiness probe failures due to containerd connection issues.
No traces were found for the checkout service, indicating a total failure of telemetry collection.

hypotheses.statement: Container runtime (containerd) instability or crash on the worker node.
hypotheses.mechanism: The mass rollout of 10+ workloads simultaneously overwhelmed containerd, leading to socket connection resets and preventing probe execution and pod management.

hypotheses.statement: Recommendations deployment has a probe misconfiguration or startup crash preventing it from serving traffic.
hypotheses.mechanism: Probes target the wrong port or path or the application fails to bind, leading to readiness probe failure and liveness probe restart loops.

hypotheses.statement: Inventory service readiness failure causes checkout to hang and time out, propagating 502s upstream to edge.
hypotheses.mechanism: Inventory pods failing readiness probes leads to empty endpoints or dropped requests, blocking checkout calls.

hypotheses.statement: Applications are timing out or blocking on synchronous HTTP telemetry calls to the deleted telemetry-collector service.
hypotheses.mechanism: The telemetry-collector service was deleted and replaced by telemetry-collector-v2, but workloads still target the old DNS name or endpoint, causing hung requests, increased p95 latency, and upstream 502 errors.

hypotheses.statement: Checkout 502s are symptoms of downstream dependency failures (Inventory/Recommendations).
hypotheses.mechanism: Readiness probe failures in inventory and recommendations caused them to be removed from service endpoints, leading to 502s at the checkout/edge layer.

hypotheses.statement: Edge/Ingress is returning 502s because checkout pods are unready or timing out.
hypotheses.mechanism: High latency in checkout (caused by dependency or telemetry issues) exceeds the edge timeout, or readiness probe failures remove pods from the load balancer, resulting in 502 Bad Gateway at the entry point.

hypotheses.statement: Telemetry collector failure causing upstream timeouts and 502s.
hypotheses.mechanism: Services updated at 12:21 are configured to send traces/metrics to telemetry-collector; if it failed or was misconfigured, synchronous telemetry calls might block or time out.
hypotheses.retired_reason: Checkout is configured to use jaeger.observability.svc directly, not the local telemetry-collector, and log search showed 0 telemetry errors.

hypotheses.statement: Services are hanging on synchronous telemetry exports to a missing or unreachable collector.
hypotheses.mechanism: The rollout updated services to use telemetry; if the collector (telemetry-collector) was deleted or renamed to v2 without updating client configs, outgoing spans might block or timeout, causing high latency and probe failures.
hypotheses.retired_reason: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT in checkout points to jaeger in observability namespace, not the renamed telemetry collector service.

alternatives.why_less_likely: Log search showed zero telemetry errors, and checkout explicitly points to an external jaeger endpoint rather than the deleted telemetry-collector.
Configuration inspection confirmed OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT points to a valid external service outside the shop namespace scope that was modified.
No connection refused or timeout errors to the telemetry-collector service were present in application logs.

uncertainty: Exact metric-level resource utilization for containerd on the worker node during the initial rollout spike due to metric scraping limitations.
Whether rolling updates can be staggered to prevent simultaneous container initialization stress.
remediation: Implement staggered rolling update strategies for dependent services to avoid simultaneous resource and container runtime pressure.
Review and tune liveness and readiness probe initial delay settings for inventory and recommendations services.
